title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit High
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the hydraulic oil temperature sensor circuit that is higher than it should be. The hydraulic oil temperature sensor tells the computer how warm the fluid in the shift and clutch hydraulic unit is.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Shifts may feel firmer or slower than normal

causes.name: Open or broken wire in the hydraulic oil temperature sensor circuit
Wire shorted to another power circuit

checks: Check the connector for pushed-out or loose pins
Check the hydraulic oil temperature sensor circuit for an open wire or a short to voltage
Test the hydraulic oil temperature sensor against the factory specification
fix: Repair the open or shorted wire or bad connector; if the wiring is good, replace the hydraulic oil temperature sensor.

title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the hydraulic oil temperature sensor keeps dropping out or jumping around, which usually points to a loose connection or a damaged wire.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Shifts may feel firmer or slower than normal
Problem may come and go, often over bumps

causes.name: Chafed wiring that opens or shorts as it moves

checks: Wiggle-test the wiring and connector while watching live data
Look for rubbed-through wiring near brackets and moving parts
fix: Repair the loose connection or damaged wire; replace the hydraulic oil temperature sensor only if it fails testing.

title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit
plain: The hydraulic unit that works the clutch and shifting on an automated manual transmission is not working as expected.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gears may be refused, slow or harsh to engage
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low hydraulic fluid or a leak

checks: Check hydraulic fluid level and look for leaks
Watch hydraulic pressure on a scan tool while the pump runs
fix: Fix any leak and refill; replace the pump or hydraulic unit if it cannot build pressure.

title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Cycling Period Too Short
plain: The hydraulic pump on an automated manual transmission is switching on again too soon, which means pressure is leaking down quickly.
symptoms: Pump may be heard running often
Transmission warning light on
Shifts may become slow or harsh
checks: Look for hydraulic fluid leaks
Check how fast pressure drops after the pump shuts off
fix: Repair the leak or replace the accumulator or hydraulic unit.

title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Loss of Pressure
plain: The hydraulic unit that works the clutch and shifting on an automated manual transmission has lost pressure.
symptoms: Car may not move or may not shift
Transmission warning light on
Clutch may not engage or release

causes.name: Pump relay, fuse or wiring fault

checks: Check fluid level and look for leaks
Check that the pump runs and its fuse and relay are good
fix: Fix the leak or replace the pump or hydraulic unit, then bleed and relearn the system.

title: Hydraulic Pump Relay Circuit/Open
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the hydraulic pump relay, which switches on the electric pump that builds pressure for the clutch and shift hydraulics.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gears may be refused, slow or harsh to engage
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the hydraulic pump relay
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the hydraulic pump relay for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the hydraulic pump relay against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the hydraulic pump relay.

title: Hydraulic Pump Relay Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The hydraulic pump relay is giving readings that don't match what the computer expects for the current conditions. The hydraulic pump relay switches on the electric pump that builds pressure for the clutch and shift hydraulics.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gears may be refused, slow or harsh to engage
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Hydraulic pump motor drawing too much current
High resistance in the wiring or connector
Control module software needs an update

checks: Compare the hydraulic pump relay reading with what it should be on a scan tool
Inspect the wiring and connector for corrosion or damage
fix: Correct any fluid or wiring problem first; if the readings are still wrong, replace the hydraulic pump relay.

title: Hydraulic Pump Relay Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the hydraulic pump relay circuit that is lower than it should be. The hydraulic pump relay switches on the electric pump that builds pressure for the clutch and shift hydraulics.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gears may be refused, slow or harsh to engage
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the hydraulic pump relay circuit

checks: Inspect the hydraulic pump relay wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the hydraulic pump relay and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the hydraulic pump relay.

title: Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning Not Complete
plain: The computer has not finished learning how the clutch and shift system behave, so shifts may not be as smooth as they should be.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Shifts or take-off may feel rough

causes.name: Adaptive learn not done after repair, battery disconnect or module replacement
Clutch or actuator problem stopping the learn from finishing
Low battery voltage during the learn

checks: Run the adaptive learn procedure with a capable scan tool
Scan for other clutch or actuator codes that block learning
fix: Complete the adaptive learn procedure; repair any fault that stops it from finishing.

title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit

symptoms: Manual or paddle shifting may not work
Check engine light on
Normal shifting in Drive usually still works

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the manual shift switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the manual shift switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion

fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the manual shift switch.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the pressure control solenoid A, which adjusts hydraulic pressure inside the transmission so the clutches apply firmly and smoothly.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Harsh, delayed or slipping shifts
Transmission may be stuck in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the pressure control solenoid
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the pressure control solenoid for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the pressure control solenoid against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the pressure control solenoid.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance

Harsh, delayed or slipping shifts
Transmission may be stuck in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Low, dirty or contaminated transmission fluid
Clogged filter or blocked hydraulic passage

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Compare the pressure control solenoid reading with what it should be on a scan tool
Inspect the wiring and connector for corrosion or damage
fix: Correct any fluid or wiring problem first; if the readings are still wrong, replace the pressure control solenoid.
drive: Drive gently to a shop soon. Pressure control problems can cause harsh, delayed or slipping shifts. If it stays in one gear, slips or flares in RPM, avoid highways and keep trips short, as slipping can damage the transmission.
test_first: Check fluid level and condition, measure the pressure control solenoid's resistance and wiring, and compare commanded versus actual current on a scanner before replacing the solenoid.

drive: Usually drivable with care to a shop soon, but shifts may be harsh, late or slipping and it may stay in one gear. Avoid highways if it won't shift right. If it slips, flares in RPM or a transmission warning appears, keep driving to a minimum or have it towed.
